evidence.observation: The dependency path from checkout-web to payment-api to auth-gateway is explicit; AUTH-2026-0318 is the recent auth-gateway change and rotated the issuer/JWKS cache namespace for partner-token validation.

At 14:10Z, checkout-web had an 18.7% HTTP 401 rate and 2400 ms p95, payment-api had a 21.2% HTTP 401 rate with the note 'auth dependency returning invalid issuer', and auth-gateway had a 28.4% HTTP 401 rate with issuer mismatch/JWKS cache-miss symptoms.
Checkout submission failed with status 401 from payment-api, and the log states that static assets were served normally while the checkout flow remained blocked.
The payment API recorded token validation failure from auth-gateway because issuer partner-v2 was not allowed, then rejected create_payment with auth_result=invalid_issuer.

After deploying AUTH-2026-0318 at 14:05:12Z, auth-gateway logged a partner-v2 JWKS cache miss, fell back to partner-v1, and rejected partner-v2 because only partner-v1 was allowed; it identified reverting the change or restoring partner-v2 as rollback candidates.

excluded_red_herrings.why_not_primary: orders-db query p95 was normal at 35 ms with zero errors, and its log says no failed checkout transaction reached the database because requests failed at the auth gate.
The metric note limits the failure to static images, while checkout-web reports static assets served normally after retry and the user-facing failure is payment authorization (HTTP 401).
Topology describes it as vacuum tuning only with no schema or credential change, and the database showed normal query latency and no errors.

recommended_next_steps: Immediately stop or roll back AUTH-2026-0318, or restore partner-v2 in auth-gateway allowed_issuers and the intended JWKS cache namespace configuration.
Invalidate/rebuild the affected JWKS cache and confirm partner-v2 tokens validate successfully before reopening checkout traffic.
Verify auth-gateway HTTP 401 rate returns to baseline, then verify payment-api and checkout-web 401 rates and p95 latency recover; exercise a complete checkout with a partner-v2 token.
Monitor orders-db and cdn-edge independently so their unrelated signals do not obscure recovery validation.
